title: Devcontainer: coding-agent toolchain, hooks, and the git wrapper
summary: This change turns the devcontainer image from a bare Rust + git-town box into a full agent workbench. It pins and installs a large toolchain (moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node 22 + pnpm, Bun, four coding agents, dsh, SkillSpector/SkillEvaluator, third-party skills), builds the repo's own dsh/omp/opencode integrations from the pnpm lockfile, and wires each agent's own hook system to `osf hook` so prompt and stop events reach the factory. It also replaces the system-wide `core.hooksPath` with a root-owned git wrapper that forces the hooks path only for repositories under the workspace, and adds build-time tests that prove the wrapper, the hooks, the agents and the skills all work for the non-root `dev` user.

lanes.subtitle: VS Code / docker

lanes.subtitle: build-time, root

lanes.subtitle: user dev, /workspace

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount + remoteEnv
nodes.summary: Now pins the bind mount to /workspace, sets workspaceFolder, forwards GH_TOKEN from the host, and extends postCreateCommand to check moon, node and pnpm as well as osf.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: +434 lines
nodes.summary: The bulk of the change: pinned downloads for moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node, Bun; global npm installs of the four coding agents; dsh from its own lockfile; SkillSpector/SkillEvaluator via uv; the repo's own dsh/omp/opencode integrations built from the pnpm lockfile; root-owned hook config for each agent; the git wrapper; and a chain of build-time tests.

nodes.label: agents.json
nodes.subtitle: the one list of agents
nodes.summary: Declares the five coding agents, their roles, which osf hook events each supports, where its hook config lives, and the gap where an agent's own hook system cannot express an osf event. The hook test reads this file instead of naming agents in code.

nodes.label: Agent hook configs
nodes.subtitle: claude-code, codex, opencode, dsh, omp
nodes.summary: Root-owned, read-only settings that point each agent's own hook system at `osf hook`: Claude Code managed settings, Codex config plus requirements and a managed hooks dir, opencode's system config naming the built plugin, dsh's factory profile, and omp's per-user hook directory.

nodes.label: .claude/hooks.json
nodes.subtitle: repo-tracked, dev-writable
nodes.summary: The Claude-format hooks bridge target for dsh's prompt event. It lives in the repository rather than under a root-owned directory because dsh resolves the bridge's configPath relative to its launch directory; agents.json records this as dsh's gap.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, then forces core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for any repository under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT before calling the real git. Replaces the previous system-wide core.hooksPath, which leaked into scratch repositories under /tmp.

nodes.label: git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Root-owned, read-only hook scripts that each call osf. The wrapper is what makes them apply under the workspace without a system-wide setting.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: The factory CLI, built from this workspace and installed read-only. It is the single command every hook and every agent hook config calls, via `osf hook prompt` and `osf hook stop`.

nodes.label: Coding agents
nodes.subtitle: dsh, omp, opencode, codex, claude
nodes.summary: Four agents installed as global npm packages plus dsh from its own lockfile. Each is usable as a builder or a reviewer; OSF_DEFAULT_BUILDER names dsh as the default.

nodes.label: dsh integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/dsh
nodes.summary: The writing-check plugin and the Claude-format hooks bridge, built from the pnpm lockfile and copied into dsh's factory profile.

nodes.label: omp integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/omp
nodes.summary: The stop hook copied into omp's per-user hooks directory; built by the same pnpm filter as dsh and opencode.

nodes.label: opencode integration
nodes.subtitle: integrations/opencode
nodes.summary: The plugin whose dist/ is copied to /opt/factory/opencode-plugin and named by opencode's system config.

nodes.label: /workspace
nodes.subtitle: bind mount of the repo
nodes.summary: The one folder the git wrapper treats as the workspace. devcontainer.json binds the repository here and OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT is set from the same build argument, so the two files never name it separately.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: /etc/profile.d
nodes.summary: Re-adds osf, the cargo toolchain and every agent binary to PATH after a login shell resets it.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 6 scripts
nodes.summary: git-wrapper, git-hooks, agent-hooks, coding-agent-tools, builder-tools, dsh-starts and skills-installed all run during the image build, so a broken wrapper, hook, agent or skill fails the build instead of shipping quietly.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image workflow
nodes.subtitle: .github/workflows
nodes.summary: CI job that builds the devcontainer image, so the pinned toolchain and the build-time tests run on every change.

nodes.label: Release hosts
nodes.subtitle: github.com, nodejs.org, npm
nodes.summary: Where moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node, Bun, the agents, dsh and the skills come from. Every download is checked against a pinned SHA-256.

nodes.label: Model APIs
nodes.subtitle: agent backends
nodes.summary: The LLM endpoints the coding agents call at run time; not touched by this change.

edges.label: reads at test time
edges.summary: The agent-hooks test copies agents.json next to itself and iterates it, so the Dockerfile never names an agent in its own test code.

edges.label: installs root-owned
edges.summary: Each agent's hook config is copied to its system-level or per-user path and made root-owned and read-only, so dev cannot repoint it.

edges.label: installs 0555
edges.summary: The wrapper is installed root-owned and read-only at /opt/factory/bin/git, ahead of the real git on PATH.

edges.label: forces core.hooksPath
edges.summary: The wrapper passes -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on every git invocation under the workspace, which is what makes the root-owned hooks apply without a system-wide setting.

edges.label: osf hook prompt|stop
edges.summary: Every agent's hook config ultimately shells out to `osf hook`, which is the single integration point this change establishes across five different hook systems.

edges.label: bridge configPath
edges.summary: dsh's Claude-format hooks bridge reads .claude/hooks.json relative to its launch directory, which is why that file stays in the repository and dev-writable.

edges.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT check
edges.summary: The wrapper only forces the hooks path when the repository sits under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, which is set from the same WORKSPACE_ROOT build argument devcontainer.json binds to.

flows.title: A coding agent's prompt hook reaches osf
flows.summary: What happens when a developer submits a prompt to any of the wired agents: the agent's own hook system invokes the command its root-owned config names, which is `osf hook prompt`.

messages.label: user_prompt_submit / UserPromptSubmit
messages.note: Claude Code, Codex and dsh's bridge all fire a prompt event; omp and opencode have no prompt event wired.

flows.title: A commit under /workspace runs the root-owned hooks
flows.summary: How the git wrapper replaces the old system-wide core.hooksPath: it inspects the repository path, and only for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT does it force the hooks path on the command line before handing off to the real git.

messages.label: is repo under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT?
messages.note: A scratch repository under /tmp is not under the workspace root, so the wrapper leaves its hooks path alone — the exact case the old system-wide setting got wrong.
